title: Drag is the same if the body moves or the fluid moves
summary: NASA Glenn says a wind past a parked wing and a wing rushing through still air are the same drag case.
body: The 'What is Drag?' page says the force comes from a difference in velocity between the solid and the air. It makes no difference which one is described as moving. A body traveling through still air, and air streaming past a body held fixed, are the same situation. The page date is 21 July 2022. The definition of drag as a contact force is a separate sentence and is not repeated here.

sources.title: What is Drag?
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 21 July 2022. Paraphrase of the relative-motion sentence.
